title: LangWatch observability and comparison

sources.supports: Parent trace and callback attached to graph invocation, including ordinary nodes, tools, and model spans.
Setup, project scope, OpenTelemetry provider, exit flushing; latest documentation differs from installed SDK.
Trace context manager and capture flags apply to the root span; callback returns child instrumentation.
Selective callbacks, inherited tags/metadata, background tracing and wait_for_all_tracers.
Hiding, masking, metadata controls, and conditional disabling are separate privacy measures.
HTTP 200 can include partial success; inspect rejected spans rather than HTTP status alone.

installed_api_observation.note: Read-only signature inspection only. Installed langwatch.setup has no project_id or flush_on_exit keyword; reuse the shared helper's environment-scoped project and provider flush instead of copying newer documentation arguments.

limitations: No live Anthropic, tracing export, service checker, or dashboard operation was performed by the module author; parent must validate these separately.
run_demo reports application checks only; the CLI tracing context attempts flush after run_demo returns and does not return a server ingestion acknowledgment.
Synthetic exact-ID retrieval is solely a tracing fixture, not semantic search or a substitute for L11 Chroma RAG.
Root capture_input/capture_output flags do not sanitize callback-generated child spans. Both tracing backends receive synthetic graph/model/tool data when selected.
The privacy plan describes the supplied runtime's selected routes, not proof of redaction or a general firewall against unrelated process instrumentation.
LangWatch checker evidence concerns its separate connection-check trace, not automatic proof that a later lesson trace was stored or displayed.
